newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO BEGINS TITLE STALK AT CANADA CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO BEGINS TITLE STALK AT CANADA CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Elvis Stojko aims to take his first steps towards reclaiming the world title at the Canadian figure skating championships this week.
The 24-year-old Stojko, who has twice been crowned national and world champion, hopes to erase the disappointment of last season and raise those counts to three this year.
Stojko says he will use this national championship as "a stepping stone for the rest of the season."
"I have goals to reach at Canadians," says Stojko. "I want to upgrade the program; to do the quad (toe) jump in combination."
A split-second miscue in the short programme cost him his world title last season and caused Stojko to step back and analyse his situation.

He decided that in his second year as world champion he had tried to please too many people and do too many things. As a result, Stojko has narrowed his focus to concentrate on what he calls "the game plan."

"The '96 (autumn) season's been great. I've had time to myself, time to relax, time to train, time to be me -- Elvis Stojko -- the guy who likes to get away with friends and train hard and sweat it out every day," he said.

"I'm not a very glamorous person. I'm the sweaty guy who goes to the rink and works out to get to the top. I'm not into the fame and glitter. There are some things I do with sponsors but I want time to focus on what I want to get done for next season," he said with an eye on 1998 Olympic gold in Nagano.

Winning the Canadian title should be easy work for Stojko. The real test of Stojko's mettle will come later this month at the Champions Series Final in Hamilton, his last test before the March world championships in Lausanne, Switzerland.

There he will face reigning world champion Todd Eldredge of the United States and Russian Alexei Urmanov. The trio skated to a three-way tie for first place in the ISU Champions Series, each winning two of the six international events.
Stojko takes to the ice Friday for the men's short programme at the Canadian championships. The final is set for Saturday evening before an expected crowd of 15,000.
Canada's other world medal contenders, Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz, are primed to take their fifth national ice dance title.
